feed.title: Self-hosted AI security advisories, checked by MV2
feed.subtitle: Which versions of Ollama, Open WebUI, vLLM, n8n, Dify, RAGFlow, AnythingLLM, Langflow, Flowise and LiteLLM are affected, including advisories with no CVE ID that scanners miss. By MV2 of Munim, Inc., with AI agents.

entry.title: Flowise is archived: 3.1.4 is the last release, and its six September advisories will never get an official fix
entry.summary: Flowise froze its code on 29 July 2026, archived the repository on 13 August and stopped taking security reports. Six advisories published on 10 September (two critical SSO takeovers, four missing-authorization bugs) affect 3.1.4, the final release on npm and Docker Hub, and none has a CVE ID or an OSV record. Fixes matching two of them were merged to main after 3.1.4 but never released. Mitigations for today (single SSO provider, one instance per team, block /admin/queues, keep port 3000 private) and how to plan a move.

entry.title: RAGFlow GHSA-c6q8: the Python fix is in 1.0.0-rc1, but rc1 serves that route from the new Go server by default
entry.summary: GHSA-c6q8-23rp-32cv still lists no patched version. Its Python fix (PR #19817, merged 18 September) is in v1.0.0-rc1 and not in v0.27.2, but 1.0.0-rc1's docker/.env sets API_PROXY_SCHEME=go, so the fix is unconfirmed for the default setup. Notes on rc1's added default services and replacing default passwords before the first start.

entry.title: Open WebUI ignores your environment variable change? It's persistent config. ENABLE_SIGNUP=false and sign-up still open
entry.summary: After the first start, Open WebUI takes settings marked ConfigVar (ENABLE_SIGNUP, DEFAULT_USER_ROLE, WEBUI_URL, ENABLE_API_KEYS, OLLAMA_BASE_URLS, JWT_EXPIRES_IN and more) from its database, not from your Compose file, because ENABLE_PERSISTENT_CONFIG defaults to True. A one-line check of /api/config shows whether sign-up is really off and whether the admin account is still unclaimed. Three fixes: the Admin Panel, RESET_CONFIG_ON_START for one start (it clears every stored setting), or ENABLE_PERSISTENT_CONFIG=False; and why OAuth works the other way round.

entry.title: Self-hosted Dify security checklist: INIT_PASSWORD, the old public SECRET_KEY, open ports and default passwords
entry.summary: Upgrades keep your .env as it was. Until 1.14.x, Dify's .env.example shipped one fixed, published SECRET_KEY, which signs login tokens; 1.15.0+ leaves it empty and auto-generates one. How to check and replace it (what logs out, what needs re-authorizing). Set INIT_PASSWORD before the first start so nobody else claims /install; nginx 80/443 and the plugin debugging port 5003 are published on every interface (bind them to 127.0.0.1 through EXPOSE_* in .env); console CORS stays * because .env.example sets it; the bundled database, Redis, sandbox and plugin keys are public defaults, and how to change the Postgres password without breaking the API. With tests.

entry.title: Langflow has no login? Turn off LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN: a self-hosted Langflow security checklist
entry.summary: A pip-installed Langflow signs everyone in as superuser (LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN defaults to True; the official Docker images set it to false) and allows any origin with credentials. Check it with one request to /api/v1/auto_login (403 = off), set LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=False with a superuser password, turn off sign-up and the superuser CLI, keep LANGFLOW_SECRET_KEY on an existing install (rotating needs the migration script), set LANGFLOW_CORS_ORIGINS and secure cookies, keep webhook auth on, decide who may run Python (custom components, sandbox, SSRF loopback), keep port 7860 on 127.0.0.1. With tests.

entry.title: LiteLLM proxy hardening checklist: master key, LITELLM_SALT_KEY, Admin UI login, EXPERIMENTAL_UI_LOGIN and MCP stdio
entry.summary: The master key is the Admin UI password unless UI_PASSWORD is set; without LITELLM_SALT_KEY, stored provider keys are encrypted with the master key, and the salt key must never change once set. Update past GHSA-7hp6, create real admin users and set disable_env_credential_login, set EXPERIMENTAL_UI_LOGIN=false if you don't use CLI SSO, leave stdio MCP servers off, keep port 4000 on 127.0.0.1 (the CLI default is 0.0.0.0), and let only the model API through Caddy or nginx while /ui and management routes stay on your network. With tests.

entry.title: ComfyUI --listen safely: from another PC or your phone without opening it to everyone
entry.summary: ComfyUI has no login, and --listen with no value binds 0.0.0.0,:: (every interface). Name the addresses instead (--listen 127.0.0.1,100.x.y.z), or keep it on localhost behind Tailscale Serve; why --enable-cors-header (any value) turns off ComfyUI's cross-site check; the "non matching host and origin" 403 behind nginx and its fix; ComfyUI-Manager security_level on a listening server; and the four CVEs fixed in 0.28.0.

entry.title: Use Ollama from another computer or your phone without exposing it: SSH tunnel, Tailscale, LAN firewall
entry.summary: Instead of OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0 or "Expose Ollama to the network": an SSH tunnel for one laptop; Open WebUI over Tailscale Serve for your phone, with Ollama kept on localhost; why tailscale serve in front of Ollama returns 403 (Ollama's Host check on loopback) and two fixes, binding to the Tailscale IP or a ufw rule for tailscale0 only; a LAN-only firewall rule for Linux and Windows; LM Studio's Require Authentication (0.4.0+).

entry.title: Open WebUI behind nginx or Caddy: fix the WebSocket and streaming errors without opening it up
entry.summary: Why /ws/socket.io fails with 403 and streamed answers arrive garbled behind a proxy, and the fix: WebSocket headers, proxy_buffering off, CORS_ALLOW_ORIGIN and WEBUI_URL set to your address, secure cookies, a fixed WEBUI_SECRET_KEY and FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS, with port 3000 on 127.0.0.1 only and your admin account created before the server is exposed. Caddy and nginx configs and tests.

entry.title: vLLM --api-key doesn't cover every endpoint: lock vLLM down with an allowlist proxy (Caddy or nginx)
entry.summary: Per vLLM's security guide, --api-key checks only /v1, /v2, /inference and /cohere routes; /invocations, /tokenize, /pause, /abort_requests and /update_weights stay open, and vllm serve listens on every interface unless --host is set. Bind to 127.0.0.1, pass only the routes your apps use through Caddy or nginx with a Bearer key, test it, and keep multi-node traffic on an isolated network.

entry.title: Self-hosted n8n security checklist: the secure cookie error, reverse proxy, n8n audit, SSRF protection and webhook auth
entry.summary: Fix "configured to use a secure cookie" with HTTPS (Caddy, N8N_PROXY_HOPS=1) instead of N8N_SECURE_COOKIE=false, keep port 5678 private, run n8n audit, keep the 2.0 defaults (N8N_BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_IN_NODE, Execute Command off, ~/.n8n-files, secure task runners), turn on N8N_SSRF_PROTECTION_ENABLED (2.12.0+), add authentication and IP allowlists to webhooks, and back up N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY. With a Compose example.

entry.title: Ollama API key: your local Ollama has none. How to require one with Caddy or nginx, and connect Open WebUI, n8n and OpenAI clients
entry.summary: OLLAMA_API_KEY is for ollama.com; the local API on port 11434 has no login. Use Open WebUI's /ollama/ route as the gate, or put Caddy or nginx in front with an exact Authorization: Bearer check, test that port 11434 can't be reached directly, and set the key in Open WebUI, n8n, the OpenAI SDK and the ollama Python library.

entry.title: Can any website talk to your local Ollama? A one-click OLLAMA_ORIGINS check (and LM Studio CORS)
entry.summary: A browser check run on your own machine: it asks 127.0.0.1:11434 and 127.0.0.1:1234 for their version from a public page, which is exactly what any website could do. If it gets an answer, OLLAMA_ORIGINS (or LM Studio's Enable CORS) is too wide. Nothing is sent anywhere. Fixes for Linux, macOS, Windows and Docker, and what Chrome's local network prompt does and doesn't cover.

entry.title: Open WebUI or n8n in Docker can't connect to Ollama: four fixes that don't expose Ollama
entry.summary: Why containers get "Connect call failed ('127.0.0.1', 11434)" or "ECONNREFUSED ::1:11434", a one-line test with a throwaway container, and fixes for Docker Desktop and Linux (host networking, host.docker.internal with a ufw rule that only lets containers in, or one Compose file) instead of opening OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0 to the whole network.

entry.title: Is my Ollama exposed? A checklist for OLLAMA_HOST, Docker ports, proxies and Open WebUI
entry.summary: Ollama's API has no login. How to check whether port 11434 is reachable from other machines and close it: OLLAMA_HOST on Linux, macOS and Windows, Docker -p 127.0.0.1 (ufw doesn't block Docker), keeping Ollama internal behind Open WebUI, a Caddy proxy with basic auth, OLLAMA_ORIGINS, and Open WebUI sign-up settings.

entry.title: Open WebUI: update to 0.12.0; the September advisories fixed in 0.11.4 still have no CVE IDs
entry.summary: Open WebUI 0.12.0 (10 October 2026) includes security and access-control fixes, some not yet published as advisories. The 15+ September advisories fixed in 0.11.4, including session-token theft from any website a signed-in user visits (GHSA-vpq8-f445-hcq7), are still not in OSV or the GitHub Advisory Database.

entry.title: Ollama CVEs in 2026, and the two that name no fixed version (CVE-2026-5757, CVE-2026-15685)
entry.summary: From 0.35.0, Ollama is past every CVE that names a fixed version, including CVE-2026-103663 (/api/pull path traversal, 8 October 2026). CVE-2026-5757 looks like the same bug as Bleeding Llama (fixed in 0.17.1), but no source confirms it. CVE-2026-15685 has no known fix.

entry.title: vLLM: 30+ advisories from 12 September to 9 October 2026, most with no CVE ID; fixed in 0.31.0
entry.summary: Five checked vLLM advisories return "not found" on OSV.dev and in the GitHub Advisory Database, so pip-audit doesn't report them. 0.31.0 fixes all of them.

entry.title: AnythingLLM: advisories that name a fix commit instead of a version, mapped to releases
entry.summary: Most 2026 AnythingLLM advisories list a commit hash or ">1.16.1" as the fix. Each fix commit was mapped to the first release containing it; 1.16.2 is past all of them.

entry.title: n8n's September 2026 advisories: 26 with no CVE ID; fixed in 2.41.4, 2.42.1 and 1.123.83
entry.summary: n8n's 16 and 30 September batches have no CVE IDs and are not in OSV or the GitHub Advisory Database, so npm audit and Dependabot can call an n8n 2.40.0 clean.
